title: How to choose a renovation crew: what to look for in the contract
seo_title: How to Choose a Renovation Crew: Contract Checklist
description: How to choose a renovation crew in Kyiv: what the contract, estimate and payment schedule must contain. Turnkey renovation from $550/m². Checklist.
lead: A renovation crew in Kyiv can be excellent or troublesome, but at the start both look the same: confident words and a pleasant price. The difference shows in the contract. Here is what to look at before you sign.
photo_alt: Living room — Tetris Hall, a CAS Development project
body: h2
Why does the contract matter more than promises?
p

When you choose a [renovation crew](/en/renovation-crew), you are buying not only the work but the order in which it is done. A verbal “we'll do it properly” guarantees nothing: if something goes wrong, all you will have is what is written on paper. So choosing a crew is essentially reading the contract and the accompanying documents.
p
Below is a list of points worth checking before signing. You can use it for a large crew, a small team or a studio running a [turnkey renovation](/en/turnkey-renovation).
h2
Who exactly is the party to the contract?
p

The first question is who you are signing with. It may be a company, a sole trader or an unregistered individual. This determines who you can bring a claim against and who is responsible for the result.
ul
the contractor's full name and details in the contract, not just the site foreman's name
the contact of the person responsible who solves problems on site
whether the crew works alone or brings in subcontractors, and who is responsible for them
p
If different people keep turning up on your site and nobody can name who is responsible for the result, that is a reason to stop.
h2
What should the scope of works and estimate include?
p
Most disputes arise over what was and was not included in the price. That is why the contract or its annex must contain a detailed list.
ul
all types of work by room with quantities (area, number of points, length)
works and materials listed separately: who buys them, with whose money, from which list
what exactly is done at the rough stage and what at the finishing stage
who removes waste and cleans the site after the works
p

Market rates vary, so focus on specific figures. At CAS Development a turnkey renovation costs from $550/m², an [office fit-out](/en/office-renovation) from $350/m². These are base rates; the final amount comes from the estimate after inspecting the property. If a crew names a sum without an inspection and without a list of works, it is only a guess.

h2
How do you tie the work schedule to payments?
p
In a proper contract, stages of work and payments are tied to each other. You pay for a completed and accepted stage, not for the whole job upfront.
ul
a timeline: which stages, in what order and when they finish
the payment procedure: what is paid before starting and what after a stage is accepted
what happens in case of delay on the part of the crew or the client
how additional works are recorded: in writing, with a separate calculation, before they are carried out
p
Read the clause on additional works especially carefully. That is usually where the difference between the initial price and the final one is hidden.
h2
How are works accepted, and what warranty applies?
p
The contract should describe how you accept the work. Without it, any claim turns into an argument about whether something was or was not done.
ul
a sign-off certificate after each stage, not only at the end
the procedure for recording defects and the deadlines for fixing them
warranty obligations: what they cover and for how long
who is responsible for concealed works closed up in walls and floors
p
The warranty must be stated as a specific period, not just “we provide a warranty”. At CAS Development the warranty on completed works is 12 months.

h2
Who reports on site, and how?
p

Even a perfect contract does not replace day-to-day control. Agree in advance how you will learn about progress: photos, short reports, site meetings. It is good when one person is responsible for your project and you can turn to them with any question.
p

Decide separately who checks the quality of concealed works: electrics, plumbing, waterproofing. They can only be checked before the walls are closed. If the renovation follows a design project, it is convenient when the author of the design also checks the execution — that is how [design project implementation](/en/design-implementation) works within one team. Our design project starts from $30/m², with a minimum of $2 500.
h2
Which warning signs should put you on guard?
ul
refusing to provide a contract or a written estimate before work starts
a price much lower than other offers with no explanation why
a demand to pay for the whole scope upfront
no address, no company details, no permanent contact
vague wording: “if needed”, “by agreement”, “as it turns out”
h2
How do you compare crews' offers by the numbers?
p

To check other offers, it helps to have your own benchmark. For a 70 m² apartment, a turnkey renovation from $550/m² gives roughly 70 × $550 = $38 500. This is a calculation at the base rate, not an offer: the exact amount is set by the estimate. If someone offers much less without a detailed list of works, ask them to explain what exactly is not included in the price.
h2
How it is organised at CAS Development
p

We start with the design and estimate and only then move on to work according to the agreed plan. One manager is responsible for your project and stays in touch throughout the renovation. You receive progress reports, and after handover a 12-month warranty. Before a meeting you can look through the [frequently asked questions](/en/faq) about prices, timescales and warranty. If you want to compare our offer with others, leave a request and we will calculate your project.
faq: What should I look for in a contract with a renovation crew?

The contractor's details, a detailed list of works with quantities, the split between works and materials, a schedule of stages with payments tied to it, the acceptance procedure and warranty obligations.
How much does a turnkey renovation cost in Kyiv?
At CAS Development a turnkey renovation costs from $550/m², an office fit-out from $350/m². The final amount is set by the estimate after inspecting the property.
Should I pay a crew upfront?
It is safer when payments are tied to stages: you pay for a completed and accepted stage. A demand to pay for the whole scope in advance is a warning sign.
What warranty is given on a renovation?
At CAS Development the warranty on completed works is 12 months. In any contract the warranty should be stated as a specific period.
